title: Lesson 2 Quiz: Public Goods and Common Resources
description: A short quiz to check what you learned in this lesson. Submitting it completes the lesson's quiz requirement, and your score is recorded separately.

history.note: AI-written question draft. Not yet reviewed by a human (admin); do not give to students.
Comprehensive audit: q5 states the maximum number of cows so the open-access count is determined. Not reviewed or approved by a human.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is closest to a public good?

choices.text: National defense that protects the country
A sandwich sold at a convenience store
A movie theater seat that requires a ticket
An amusement park pass that you pay for

questions.prompt: How are fish on the high seas, waters outside any country's jurisdiction, best classified?

choices.text: A public good, because no one can be kept out and sharing does not use it up
A private good, because whoever catches the fish gets to keep them
A good with no externality, because the people fishing do not trade with each other
A common resource, because anyone can fish but each catch leaves fewer fish for others

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: Renovating the park in a neighborhood of 50 households costs $10,000. All households share the park, and each household values it at $250. What is the social net benefit of the renovation (social value − cost), in dollars? (Enter a number only.)
What is the main reason markets tend not to supply enough public goods?

choices.text: Because public goods cost nothing to produce
Because nonpayers still benefit, so each person avoids paying
Because very few people want public goods
Because when one person uses a public good, others cannot use it

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: On a village's shared pasture, total daily income by number of cows grazing is $20 for 1 cow, $36 for 2, $48 for 3, $56 for 4, and $60 for 5. Keeping one cow costs $10 per day, and at most 5 cows can graze there. If anyone can graze cows there, cows keep being added as long as the average income is at least the cost. How many dollars less is the net income (total income − cost) than at the efficient number of cows? (Enter a number only.)
